overview: This Senate resolution marks the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks and honors the 2,977 people killed in New York, at the Pentagon, and in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. It thanks the firefighters, police, medical workers, troops, intelligence staff, and volunteers who responded, and honors the passengers and crew of United Airlines Flight 93. It also recognizes service members, veterans, and Gold Star families (families who lost a loved one in military service), and the charities that still support survivors and victims' families. It encourages Americans to mark the day with ceremonies and to carry on the spirit of unity and service seen after the attacks. It does not change any law or spending. As of September 16, 2026, the Senate had agreed to it.
for: Supporters say a formal statement on the 25th anniversary honors the victims and responders and keeps the commitment to remember the attacks.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
